Five things the grid format cannot express yet, found by building it once
why: The prototype rendered cleanly on the first attempt, so the remaining questions are not about whether the mechanism works. They are about what the DSL leaves the author unable to say, or unable to see. Each needs a decision before the format is worth extending to the full 21-card diagram.
subtree: 16 cards, 1 open, 15 decided, 1 unchallenged, 1 stale

Ordered by how much they threaten the design, not by how hard they are.

**1. A lane is not centred in the card it leaves, and the author cannot see that.**
`mv` spans columns 0 to 2 and its lane is column 1, but equal distribution across a span does not cancel column 1s 26px lane baseline, so the lane sits about 25px left of the card centre. Every line in the render leaves its card visibly off-centre.
This is the one that matters, because the entire argument for this design is that the grid is legible to its own author before rendering. Here it is not: the information is present (lane at column 1 of a 0-2 span is left of middle) but it takes counting to see, and the consequence is invisible.
Cheapest fix, and it keeps the property: a checker rule. "Edge X attaches to card Y off-centre" as a warning. The author still cannot see it, but no longer has to.

**2. Group frames are metric and the grid reserves no space for them.**
A frame needs a header strip above its top card. BROWSER is in row 0, so its frame computed to y = -4 and the whole drawing had to be shifted afterwards to compensate. Worse, the SERVER PROCESS top border currently crosses row 4s lane cells, and its header text misses the vertical line by luck.
A group is a first-class thing in the content section but has no cells of its own. Either it gets them (a `browser` token that fills its frame cells, so the author sees and controls the header strip), or rows gain a declared type. Undecided.

**3. A wide label sits further from its own line than a narrow one.**
A label is centred in its own cell box, so the two-cell `@lv_cp` puts its text about 55px from the line it belongs to, while the one-cell `@cp_lv` reads tight against it. More cells means further away, which is backwards from what an author intends by spending more cells.
Fix is small: a label box should hug the side of its box nearest its own lane, not centre in it.

**4. An empty column collapses to zero width.**
There is no token meaning "a gap of at least N here". The only way to buy horizontal air is to put something in the column. On a four-card diagram this never bites; on 21 cards it will.

**5. The derived edge id is ambiguous.**
`<from>_<to>` collides with any node id containing an underscore, and `a_b -> c` and `a -> b_c` both produce `a_b_c`. The implementation resolves a bare token as a card first, then an edge, which is a guess, not a rule.
Better: make the grid token `mv->st` rather than `mv_st`. Unambiguous, and it reads as what it is. Costs two characters per cell.
